response.justification: Bogdan is an experienced, versatile senior engineer with genuine geospatial credentials (GISCollective, Green Map web GIS, FOSS4G talk) and some high-throughput, low-latency backend work at Sociomantic/Dunnhumby (async I/O, fibers, caching, millions of req/s). However, the role's primary hard requirement — modern C++ (or Rust) in commercial or open-source settings — is only weakly met: his C/C++ exposure is a ~7-month stint at National Instruments in 2014–2015 plus a university thesis, with no evidence of modern C++ (C++17/20) or Rust. The last decade has been predominantly TypeScript/Node.js and D, and there is no experience with routing tiles, navigation guidance, or map data pipelines. He could plausibly ramp up given his systems-level D work and stated appetite for learning across the stack, but he would not be a mid-senior hire who is productive on the core codebase quickly. Worth a screening call only if the team is open to a strong generalist who must learn modern C++ on the job.
strengths: Real geospatial/GIS product experience (GISCollective, Open Green Map, FOSS4G speaker)
Low-latency, high-throughput distributed backend work at Sociomantic (async I/O, fibers, caching)
Strong engineering discipline: TDD, CI/CD, own test tooling, Linux and DevOps depth
concerns: Modern C++ experience is minimal and ~10 years stale; no Rust at all
No navigation, routing, or map-tiling pipeline experience
Recent decade is web/full-stack TypeScript, not systems-level performance engineering
